[RARC.5.1] An engine is the network compiled from one rule set, together with
its clock source ([RARC.5.5]), working memory ([RARC.5.2]), agenda
([RARC.5.4]) and dispatcher ([RARC.5.7]). The integrator drives it through
public calls — assert, retract, the clock operations and pump — and each call
is processed serially to completion before it returns ([RARC.5.6]). The engine
has no thread, queue or loop of its own. Everything it does that an integrator
can observe reaches the integrator through its callbacks: the stream callback
for every observable event ([RARC.5.8]), and the typed callbacks for the
actions the dispatcher routes.
